Q0654

“So long as the field of separation between within and without is…” — Nishitani Keiji (Q0654)

An English quotation associated with Religion and Nothingness (Van Bragt, p. 10), organized here under self.

Quotes / Nishitani Keiji / Q0654

English

So long as the field of separation between within and without is not broken through, and so long as a conversion from that standpoint does not take place, the lack of unity and contradiction spoken of earlier cannot help but prevail among the things we take as real.
Thinker Nishitani Keiji
School Kyoto School
Source Religion and Nothingness (Van Bragt, p. 10)
Theme Self
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Religion and Nothingness (Van Bragt, p. 10), within the Kyoto School tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of self, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Nishitani Keiji's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
